title: International Space Station
content: The International Space Station is a large human-made orbital laboratory. It operates in low Earth orbit and supports scientific research, technology development and international cooperation in space.

title: Earth Observation Data
content: NASA Earthdata provides access to NASA Earth science data and resources. Earth observation data can be used to study the atmosphere, land, oceans, climate and other Earth system processes.

title: Catalog of Earth Satellite Orbits
content: Satellites operate in different types of Earth orbits. Low Earth orbit is commonly used by scientific and Earth-observation satellites. Geostationary orbit allows a satellite to remain approximately over the same region of Earth and is useful for continuous weather monitoring.

title: Space Radiation
content: Space radiation includes high-energy particles such as galactic cosmic rays and particles associated with solar storms. Radiation can affect astronauts and spacecraft, so NASA studies and monitors the radiation environment and develops protection approaches.

title: How NASA Prepares Spacecraft for Radiation
content: Spacecraft encounter different radiation environments depending on their destination. Engineers consider solar particles, radiation belts and galactic cosmic rays when selecting and testing spacecraft components for a mission.

title: Spacecraft Attitude Control
content: A spacecraft's attitude is its orientation in space. Attitude control stabilizes and controls the spacecraft so its high-gain antenna can point accurately toward Earth for communications, scientific instruments can point correctly to collect data, thermal conditions can be managed, and propulsive maneuvers can be performed in the correct direction.

title: Science Instruments and Spacecraft Payloads
content: Science instruments are carried by spacecraft to collect scientific data and perform observations or experiments. Instruments are integrated with the spacecraft and tested to verify commands, telemetry, power, thermal and mechanical requirements. Different instruments have different purposes and can include remote-sensing and direct-sensing systems.

title: Earth Observation and Disaster Response
content: NASA uses Earth observation data to support disaster planning, response and recovery. Satellite observations can provide information about hazards and affected areas, helping decision-makers and response teams understand disaster impacts. NASA provides Earth observation data, analysis and tools for events such as floods, fires, hurricanes, landslides and other hazards.

title: NASA Space Missions
content: NASA conducts human spaceflight, science and space technology missions. Science missions study Earth, the Sun, the Moon, Mars and other destinations. Space technology missions demonstrate technologies and capabilities for future science and exploration missions.

title: Spacecraft Instruments
content: Spacecraft use different instruments because missions have different scientific objectives and observation requirements. Instruments can provide complementary capabilities for studying Earth's atmosphere, environmental conditions and other targets. Instrument selection depends on what a mission needs to measure and observe.
